claims.claim_text_verbatim: To address this, we propose Hippocam, a hierarchical memory and continual learning architecture.
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam is a hierarchical memory and continual learning architecture for LLM agents.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Through this memory dynamic of use and disuse, Hippocam connects working context, long-term memory, knowledge accumulation, and skill learning within a single continuously evolving experiential process.
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam unifies context management, memory, knowledge, and skill learning via use and disuse.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This enables agents to learn and evolve capabilities through their own experiences without parameter updates.
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam allows agents to continuously evolve capabilities without updating model weights.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Whereas competing methods show more uneven performance across these demands, Hippocam leads or matches the best compared method on seven of the eight measures in Fig. 1.
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam matches or beats top baselines on 7 out of 8 evaluated benchmark metrics.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Hippocam does not build a memory bank separate from its interaction history, but remembers and learns by deliberately maintaining its context.
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam manages memory directly within context rather than using a separate memory bank.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Both forms of consolidation keep the agent’s recent context focused and high-signal, enabling accurate and coherent reasoning over long horizons.
claims.claim_summary: Consolidation keeps working context concise and high-signal for long-horizon reasoning.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Experience that remains unused continues to recede in detail through recursive consolidation, without separately assigned importance scores or time-based forgetting rules.
claims.claim_summary: Unused details recede naturally without explicit importance scores or decay rules.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This natural dynamic of use and disuse unifies the recovery of past experience with learning that deepens what the agent knows, refines how it acts, and expands what it can accomplish.
claims.claim_summary: Use and disuse dynamics unify memory recall with continuous learning and capability expansion.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Hippocam improves across all three benchmarks, achieving 97.8% ALFWorld success and tying ACE for the best result.
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam reaches 97.8% success on ALFWorld, tying the top baseline.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Its 81.9% mean ScienceWorld progress exceeds four of the six compared methods.
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam achieves 81.9% mean progress on ScienceWorld, outperforming most baselines.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On StreamBench, it achieves the highest mean accuracy of 81.7%, narrowly ahead of Letta’s 81.3%.
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam hits 81.7% mean accuracy on StreamBench, outperforming all competitors.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On DDXPlus, Hippocam continues to improve after early fluctuations and maintains its lead, while Letta and A-Mem also improve.
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam maintains leading accuracy on DDXPlus as experience accumulates over time.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On ToolBench, Hippocam makes modest further gains amid fluctuations and moves ahead of Letta, whereas A-Mem shows little sustained improvement in the extended evaluation.
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam advances past Letta on ToolBench with extended interaction tasks.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: In both streams, Hippocam also achieves higher accuracy with about 10% lower average cost per task in the later 150-task interval (§ A.9).
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam improves accuracy while cutting per-task cost by 10% in later task streams.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Hippocam achieves 78.9% mean progress, improving over Plain by 30.1 pp and exceeding the strongest baseline, ACE, by 16.2 pp.
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam reaches 78.9% frozen transfer progress on ScienceWorld, beating ACE by 16.2 points.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On FEVER, Frozen scores cluster around Plain’s 59.3%, with Hippocam and HiAgent reaching 61.8%.
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam achieves 61.8% accuracy on FEVER under frozen cross-domain evaluation.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Only Hippocam and ACE achieve positive gains on both domain transitions, while the remaining methods show mixed, unchanged, or reduced performance.
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam and ACE are the only methods showing consistent positive gains across both cross-domain transitions.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Hippocam achieves larger gains of 19.2 and 6.0 pp, respectively, with a narrower FEVER gap under the scoring sensitivity analysis (§ A.2).
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam shows substantial positive domain transfer gains on ScienceWorld (+19.2 pp) and FEVER (+6.0 pp).

claims.claim_text_verbatim: In contrast, Hippocam maintains high performance in both conditions without degradation under interleaving, scoring 85.1% in isolation and 88.7% under interleaving (Fig. 5, left).
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam resists task interference, scoring 85.1% in isolation and 88.7% when tasks are interleaved.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On LoCoMo, Hippocam achieves 77.6% overall accuracy, exceeding the strongest baseline, A-Mem, by 10.1 pp (Table 3).
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam hits 77.6% overall accuracy on LoCoMo, beating A-Mem by 10.1 percentage points.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: It leads or ties across all four answerable question categories, with temporal accuracy reaching 86.6% compared with A-Mem’s 67.6%.
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam leads on all answerable LoCoMo categories, reaching 86.6% on temporal questions.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Hippocam combines stronger conversational reasoning with 87.2% accuracy on unanswerable questions.
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam achieves 87.2% accuracy on adversarial unanswerable questions in LoCoMo.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Across the three input lengths, Hippocam achieves 71.7% mean accuracy, compared with 44.3% for Letta (Fig. 5, right).
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam averages 71.7% accuracy on MemoryAgentBench conflict resolution versus Letta's 44.3%.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: It matches HiAgent at 97.0% on 6k inputs and retains 77.0% and 41.0% accuracy at 32k and 64k, where no baseline exceeds 37.0% and 19.0%, respectively.
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam outperforms baselines at long contexts, reaching 77% at 32k and 41% at 64k inputs.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Hippocam combines this breadth with stronger overall performance, leading or tying on seven of the eight measures.
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam offers broader domain capability while leading or tying on 7 of 8 benchmark metrics.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On GoodAI, filler retention rises from 14% to 63%, while scores fall by 23.1 pp under interleaving versus 7.3 pp in isolation (Table 4).
claims.claim_summary: Removing intent conditioning increases filler retention and significantly lowers GoodAI task scores.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Prefix consolidation thus supports more effective subsequent work with a smaller active context.
claims.claim_summary: Prefix consolidation maintains task efficiency while drastically shrinking working context size.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Disabling recall on the same post-ingestion MemoryAgentBench 64k snapshot reduces accuracy from 41.0% to 27.0%.
claims.claim_summary: Disabling progressive recall drops MemoryAgentBench 64k accuracy from 41.0% to 27.0%.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Access to underlying evidence therefore improves reasoning beyond what the consolidated context alone supports.
claims.claim_summary: Progressive recall of raw evidence enhances reasoning performance over summarized context alone.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: These cases show that Hippocam adapts retrieval depth to the task, recovering sufficient evidence without expanding the entire history.
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam dynamically adjusts retrieval depth, pulling only necessary evidence from history.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Across both streams, Hippocam’s later interval has higher accuracy and about 10% lower mean cost per task (Table 12).
claims.claim_summary: In extended tasks, Hippocam increases accuracy while lowering per-task inference costs by ~10%.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Its cost per correct answer is consequently lower under the stated prices (0.0173 versus 0.0271 USD).
claims.claim_summary: Hippocam achieves lower cost per correct answer ($0.0173) than A-Mem ($0.0271) on ToolBench.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Evaluations show that Hippocam achieves strong performance across memory, knowledge use, and learning.
claims.claim_summary: Evaluations show that Hippocam achieves strong performance across memory, knowledge use, and learning.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Ablations and case analyses further show how consolidation and progressive recall support ongoing work and how knowledge develops through use and disuse.
claims.claim_summary: Ablations and case analyses further show how consolidation and progressive recall support ongoing work and how knowledge develops through use and disuse.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: These results demonstrate how our use-and-disuse cycle supports memory and learning through interaction history.
claims.claim_summary: These results demonstrate how our use-and-disuse cycle supports memory and learning through interaction history.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This nested chain organizes the multiple purposes jointly served by ongoing work in a form aligned with the linear context of LLM agents.
claims.claim_summary: This nested chain organizes the multiple purposes jointly served by ongoing work in a form aligned with the linear context of LLM agents.

claims.claim_summary: This selective consolidation reduces distraction, supports coherent reasoning, and keeps the context focused and efficient, while preserving the information needed to build on established results without repeating prior work.

claims.claim_summary: PALIM consolidates these prefixes to reduce interference from less relevant details and keep the context focused on ongoing work.
